title: When a Vehicle Purchase Agreements Hold Lapses: Release, Forfeiture and Deposit Refund
content:
A reserved deal under the **Vehicle Purchase Agreements** whose hold has run out without a signed buyer's order is released, and the vehicle returns to stock.

## Release timing
A hold is released only on or after the first calendar day following the deal's hold expiry date. The hold covers the whole expiry date. Calendar days are added to the hold expiry date, and release is possible from 1 calendar day after it onward.

| Handling date, measured from the hold expiry date | Release |
|---|---|
| the expiry date itself | not yet: the hold still covers that whole day |
| 1 calendar day after the expiry date | may be released |
| any later day | may be released |

The evidence is the hold expiry date on the deal's record, including any extensions granted.

## Deposit on release
- Where the deal type keeps the non-refundable portion when a hold lapses, the store retains that portion, but never more than the deposit held. It is booked as one forfeiture against the earliest deposit, and the rest is refunded.
- Where the deal type does not keep it, the whole deposit held is refunded.
- Each deposit is refunded separately with the payment method of that deposit, within the deal type's refund period in calendar days after the release date.

## Hypothetical illustration
A deal type that keeps a non-refundable portion of 500.00 on lapse, holding a single deposit of 1200.00: on release 500.00 is retained as one forfeiture against that deposit, and 700.00 is refunded by that deposit's method. Had only 300.00 been held, the retention would be 300.00 and nothing would be refunded. On a deal type that does not keep the portion, the whole 1200.00 would be refunded.
